issues.description: The script uses GM_xmlhttpRequest to communicate with third-party APIs (SponsorBlock and multiple Cobalt instances) for segment skipping and video downloading. These requests may include YouTube video IDs and possibly other metadata, which could be considered user data.
issues.location: CFG.sbApi, CFG.cobaltInstances, and related logic (network requests to sponsor.ajay.app, co.wuk.sh, cobalt.api.timelessnesses.me, api.cobalt.tools)
issues.recommendation: Document all data sent to third-party APIs. Consider proxying requests or informing users about privacy implications. Limit data to only what is strictly necessary.

issues.description: The script stores and retrieves user toggle settings (ad skip, SponsorBlock, quality) using GM_setValue/GM_getValue. While this is local, it does not appear to collect sensitive data. No evidence of reading cookies, clipboard, or keylogging.
issues.recommendation: Ensure no sensitive user data is stored or transmitted. Document what is stored for transparency.

issues.description: The script requests GM_xmlhttpRequest permission, which is necessary for cross-origin API calls, but does not request other high-risk permissions. No evidence of unused high-privilege grants.
issues.recommendation: Keep permissions minimal and only request those strictly necessary.

issues.description: No evidence of eval, new Function, setTimeout(string), setInterval(string), or dynamic script injection. No obfuscation or minified code detected.
issues.recommendation: Maintain code clarity and avoid introducing dynamic code execution.

issues.description: The script does not appear to introduce DOM XSS or inject untrusted user input into the DOM. No use of innerHTML/outerHTML with untrusted data.
issues.recommendation: Continue to avoid inserting untrusted data into the DOM without sanitization.

issues.description: @require is not used; all code is local. No supply chain risk from external libraries.
issues.recommendation: If adding @require in the future, use only official, version-pinned sources.

details: Stores toggle settings (ad skip, SponsorBlock, quality) locally via GM_setValue/GM_getValue

script_name: EasyTube V3 — Ad Skip, SponsorBlock & HD Download⬇️🚀
summary: The script is generally well-structured and does not use obfuscation, dynamic code execution, or introduce DOM XSS. The main security concern is the transmission of YouTube video IDs and possibly other metadata to third-party APIs (SponsorBlock and Cobalt instances) for ad skipping and video downloading. No evidence of sensitive privacy data collection or supply chain risk. Permissions are appropriate for the functionality. Users should be aware of the privacy implications of using third-party APIs for SponsorBlock and video download.
